title: Plank two scaffold bays: lap the boards over the middle putlog, ends 19-38 mm out
instruction: Plank both scaffold bays with the two orange boards in one straight run: lay one board across each bay on the grey putlogs, lap the two boards over the middle putlog, and leave every board end 19 to 38 mm past the centre line of the last putlog under it.
context: Scaffold erectors and construction laborers (O*NET 47-2061) plank a scaffold's working platform board by board, to US rule 29 CFR 1926.451(b): each board end extends over the centre line of its support at least 6 in ((b)(4)); an end of a board 10 ft or shorter extends over its support no more than 12 in, or it tips up when stepped on, a 'trap end' ((b)(5)(i)); and where boards overlap to make a long platform, the overlap is only over a support and at least 12 in ((b)(7)). Here, at 1:8 scale, two boards must plank two bays as one straight run: each spans its own bay with both ends 19 to 38 mm (6 to 12 in) past their putlogs (transoms), the second lapped on the first over the middle putlog. A 250 mm board on a 190 mm bay has 60 mm of overhang to share between its ends, so it must sit within 8 mm of centred along the run.
setup: Bimanual YAM station; the table top is the reference height. x points forward from the line through the two arm bases, y to the left of the midpoint between them, z up from the table top; the arm bases are at y +30.5 cm and y -30.5 cm. A 1:8 scale model of two bays of a scaffold platform; the run of the platform is along y. Two kinds of thing are on the table. (1) Putlogs (transoms): three fixed galvanised-steel square bars, 120 mm long (along x) and 20 x 20 mm in section (about 0.38 kg each), fastened down on the table with their length along x, centred at x 26.0 cm and y +19.0 cm (left putlog), 0 (middle putlog) and -19.0 cm (right putlog). They span x 20.0 to 32.0 cm, their tops are 20 mm above the table, and their centre lines are 190 mm apart along y: the left bay lies between the left and middle putlogs, the right bay between the middle and right putlogs (each bay is 1.52 m, 5 ft, at full scale). (2) Scaffold boards: two loose pine boards painted orange, each 250 mm long, 40 mm wide and 16 mm thick (2.0 m, 6.6 ft, at full scale), 80 g, with flat faces; a board's two 250 x 40 mm faces are alike. They lie flat on the table on a 250 x 40 mm face with their length along x, centred at x 24.5 cm, y +32.0 cm (left board) and y -32.0 cm (right board), one in front of each arm. Laid centred across a bay, a board's ends are 30 mm past both putlogs' centre lines; the two 30 mm inner ends over the middle putlog make a 60 mm lap. Nothing else is on the table.
scoring: Judged on the end state from the boards' poses (in a real trial: a tape along each board from the centre line marked on each putlog's side, and a top and a side photo). A board 'lies on' a putlog when its underside comes within 2 mm of the putlog's top where the two overlap seen from above (at least 20 square mm); it also lies on a putlog 'through' the other board when it rests on that board (its underside within 2 mm of that board's top where they overlap) where that board lies on the putlog, with the putlog's centre line passing under their overlap. A board is 'on the scaffold' when it lies on at least one putlog, its long side seen from above is within 45 degrees of the run (y) and its lowest point is at least 5 mm above the table. A board end's 'overhang' is the distance along the board, toward that end, from where its centre line crosses the centre line of the last putlog it lies on to the end face. 'Still' means neither end of the board moved more than 2 mm in the last 0.5 s. A board 'planks' a bay when it lies on both of that bay's putlogs, its long side is within 5 degrees of the run, its broad faces are tilted at most 8 degrees from level (the lapped board slopes about 5.4), its outline seen from above stays within the putlogs' length (x 20.0 to 32.0 cm), both its overhangs are 19 to 38 mm, and it is still. Score 0 if any board on the scaffold has an overhang over 38 mm (a trap end): for example a board resting on one putlog only, the second board held level on the first one's end, or a flat board more than 8 mm off centre along the run in its bay. Otherwise: 1.0 if each bay is planked by a different board, the two boards' centre lines cross the middle putlog's centre line within 10 mm of each other in x (in line), and one board rests on the other over the middle putlog (lapped; the lap, both inner overhangs added, is then at least 38 mm); 0.5 if each bay is planked by a different board but they are not lapped in line (side by side, or more than 10 mm out of line); 0.25 if exactly one bay is planked (including both boards across the same bay); 0 in every other case (nothing planked: boards left on the table, held more than 2 mm above the putlogs, standing on an edge, lying along a putlog, or with one end on the table). Possible scores: 0, 0.25, 0.5, 1.0. Either board may go in either bay and either may be the upper one; boards not on the scaffold are ignored. The trial ends early, at 1.0, once 1.0 has held for 1 s; otherwise it is scored as it stands at the run limit (a 1.0 state there counts even if it has held less than 1 s). The scorer reads only the boards, not the grippers: a board still held is scored where it lies.
fidelity: Rigid boxes with the simulator's default friction; the putlogs are fixed. About 1:8 scale. The boards are 16 mm thick so a gripper can hold them (true 1:8 is 6 mm), so the lapped board slopes about 5.4 degrees, not 1 to 2; real lapped boards would also be tied or bevelled. The putlogs are square bars, not tubes; no standards, ledgers or couplers. The trap-end rule is scored from geometry (no load test). The scorer reads only the boards: a board still held is scored where it lies.
reset_notes: Put both boards back flat on the table, length along x, centred at x 24.5 cm, y +32.0 cm and y -32.0 cm. The putlogs are fixed. Nothing is consumed.
